title: CoGen: A Two-Stage Unified Multi-modal Framework for Bundle Construction via Discrete Semantics Transfer

problem.claim: Bundle construction assembles mutually compatible item sets that satisfy user preferences, including bundle completion and personalized bundle generation.

gap.claim: Existing methods isolate completion and generation; compatibility representations are difficult to transfer, while generation suffers from sparse supervision and lacks explicit compatibility constraints.

contributions.claim: CoGen is a two-stage unified multi-modal framework for bundle construction.
CoGen transfers compatibility-aware continuous representations from completion into discrete semantics for guiding bundle generation.
CoGen uses a semantic-anchored non-autoregressive generator to produce bundles from learned discrete semantics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four public multi-modal datasets reportedly verify CoGen's effectiveness against several state-of-the-art approaches.

narrative_sequence.summary: Bundle construction seeks compatible, preference-satisfying item sets and comprises completion and generation tasks.
Existing approaches separate the tasks, creating transfer, supervision, and compatibility-constraint limitations.
CoGen unifies the tasks by transferring compatibility-aware representations into discrete semantics.
The framework learns disentangled multi-modal representations, performs completion, discretizes representations with residual quantization, and generates bundles non-autoregressively.
The authors report comparative experiments on four public multi-modal datasets.

source_observation.claim: The framework makes compatibility patterns reusable for generation by discretizing completion representations into explicit semantics.

interpretation.claim: A discrete intermediate representation can serve as a transfer interface between coupled prediction and generation tasks.

application.claim: For systems combining compatibility modeling with generation, consider designing an explicit reusable semantic interface between the stages.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when discrete semantics outperform continuous transfer or whether this pattern generalizes beyond bundle construction.

unknowns: The abstract does not report dataset names, evaluation metrics, numerical results, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not specify the model architecture, loss functions, quantization configuration, or baseline identities.
The abstract does not provide ablation results or independent verification.
